artifact.type: frozen iOS Simulator build and accessibility evidence

scenario: On an iPhone 17 Simulator, review synthetic TS-CORE-01 from identity and exact evidence through fact decisions, separate action preview, local no-external-write outcome, cancellation, failure, and recovery, while attempting a truthful direct VoiceOver proof.

review_plan.reason: This bounded retest owns iOS accessibility behavior, Dynamic Type, dark mode, focus, control exposure, and recovery proof.
No evidence model, identity binding, retention behavior, permission boundary, or external-write authority changed; the frozen Round 3 safety decision remains authoritative.
Core touch task completion was rerun only to support the accessibility proof; no new uncoached recruiter evidence was collected.
No candidate-facing content, automation, communication, or consent behavior changed.
The artifact contains no candidate assessment, score, ranking, fit, personality, protected-trait, or acceptance claim.

reviews.lens: mobile task completion, visual hierarchy, accessibility, and recovery

findings.observation: The iOS 26.1 Simulator image exposed no VoiceOver setting in Accessibility and no VoiceOver option through simctl, so this run observed neither spoken output nor a VoiceOver focus ring or gesture traversal.
findings.evidence: docs/evaluations/round-4/ios/accessibility-trace.json records the direct Settings and simctl availability checks, the one Computer Use accessibility-tree order, and every VoiceOver behavior that remains unproven.
findings.user_impact: Accessible element order and touch behavior are supported, but a VoiceOver user may still encounter unclear repeated control labels, lost focus after state transitions, or incomplete exact-effect and recovery announcements.
findings.recommendation: Run the same frozen journey on a real iPhone or an environment that exposes VoiceOver, without substituting an accessibility tree transcript.
findings.verification: VoiceOver directly announces identity, provenance, evidence, proposal status, contextual confirm/edit/dismiss controls, exact-effect preview, no-external-write outcome, cancellation, failure, and retry in logical order; focus remains contained and returns predictably after every transition.

strengths: The current-source unit suite passed and the isolated Release simulator build succeeded.
The corrected focused AX5 audit passed 1/1, and the final full iOS UI suite passed 12/12 with zero failures or skips.
Passing dark-mode AX5 screenshots show the full proposal-review instruction, evidence, decision controls, status-bar clearance, and viewport-edge behavior.
The frozen TS-CORE-01 UI test passed evidence review, four confirmations, a separate exact-effect action preview, and a local no-external-write outcome.

The final full suite passed evidence-before-decision order, cancellation, failure recovery, background interruption, stale-preview blocking, scoring refusal, localhost sync, and unrelated-image isolation.
The canonical-backend test passed in the final full suite after the governed synthetic state was materialized.

Computer Use directly exposed candidate identity, source, time, exact observed evidence, each proposal and evidence quote, confirm/edit/dismiss controls, decision state, and cancellation in evidence-first order.
missing_evidence: A true VoiceOver transcript and visible focus trace for confirm, edit, dismiss, action preview, outcome, cancellation, failure, and retry.
Assistive-technology user evidence and the smallest-supported-iPhone layout run.
open_questions: Will repeated generic Confirm, Edit, Dismiss, Proposed, and Awaiting review announcements provide enough context when heard linearly?
Where does VoiceOver focus land after confirming a fact, saving or cancelling an edit, dismissing a fact, entering action preview, returning to review, and recovering from failure?

top_findings.reason: The authorized Simulator environment exposed no VoiceOver setting or simctl control, so tree order cannot be promoted to spoken assistive-technology evidence.
top_findings.next_step: Run the frozen journey on a real iPhone or another environment that actually exposes VoiceOver.
top_findings.verification: One direct trace proves spoken labels, values, hints, swipe order, contextual actions, focus containment, transition focus, exact effect, no-external-write outcome, cancellation, failure, and retry.

agreements: The current Release binary matches the frozen source and preserves the evidence-first touch journey.
Backend canonical-state failure was resolved by materializing the expected governed synthetic state; it is not an iOS binary defect.
The AX5 false positive was localized to an element clamped at the viewport edge; the corrected focused audit and full UI suite both pass.
An accessibility tree is supporting evidence and is not a substitute for VoiceOver speech, focus, or gesture proof.
No candidate data or external contact, calendar, message, ATS, CRM, or other write was used.
adjudication.rationale: This bounded retest directly proves current-source unit, Release, 12/12 UI behavior, AX5 dark mode, core touch, recovery, accessible order, and prepared-backend behavior. It cannot approve full accessibility release readiness because true VoiceOver was unavailable. The result is therefore pass_with_changes with release_gate=needs_evidence, while the prior AX5 finding is resolved.

next_tests.test: Traverse the frozen TS-CORE-01 journey with real VoiceOver.
next_tests.evidence_required: Spoken transcript or recording plus visible focus trace for identity, source, evidence, proposals, confirm, edit, dismiss, action preview, outcome, cancellation, failure, and retry.
next_tests.pass_condition: Each state and control is announced once in evidence-first order, repeated controls are contextually clear, focus remains contained and returns predictably, and no external-effect language is ambiguous.
